description: Unified Tools Configuration - Separate 1-on-1 and Group Chat Tools

one_on_one_tools.name: Gen Z Response
one_on_one_tools.description: Generates casual, Gen Z/Gen Alpha style responses. Always responds to every message in 1-on-1 chats. Uses 2-4 messages like real texts. Responds naturally to any user message with authentic Gen Z slang, abbreviations, and energy. This is the default response tool for all 1-on-1 messages.
one_on_one_tools.example_usage: User sends any message → Bot responds with Gen Z style (2-4 messages)
one_on_one_tools.when_to_use: Use this for every 1-on-1 message. This is the default conversation tool.

one_on_one_tools.name: Extract Interests
one_on_one_tools.description: Automatically extracts user interests from messages using AI. Tracks interests over time for personalization and group matching. Detects when users mention things they like, love, enjoy, or are passionate about. Extracts hobbies, preferences, favorite things, and activities. Stores interests for future reference and group matching.
one_on_one_tools.example_usage: User says 'I love pizza' → Bot extracts 'pizza' as interest
one_on_one_tools.when_to_use: Always runs automatically on every message to track user interests.

one_on_one_tools.name: Music Recommendation
one_on_one_tools.description: Automatically shares Taylor Swift song links when user shows interest in music. Always shows music link (100% probability) when music interest detected. Detects music-related keywords like 'music', 'song', 'taylor swift', 'spotify', 'apple music', 'listening', 'playlist', 'album', 'artist', 'band'. Sends 4 messages: excitement message, question about vibes, 'listening to this rn', and the song link.
one_on_one_tools.example_usage: User likes music → Bot sends 4 messages with song recommendation
one_on_one_tools.when_to_use: Automatically triggers when user has music interest or mentions music-related keywords.

parameters.returns: list of messages with music link added

one_on_one_tools.name: Voice Transcription
one_on_one_tools.description: Transcribes voice messages using Whisper AI. Processes transcribed text as regular messages. Handles audio attachments in various formats (m4a, mp3, wav, etc.). Converts speech to text and then processes the text as a normal message. Essential for accessibility and processing voice input.
one_on_one_tools.example_usage: User sends voice message → Bot transcribes and processes
one_on_one_tools.when_to_use: Automatically triggers when message contains audio/voice attachments.

one_on_one_tools.name: Auto Reaction
one_on_one_tools.description: Automatically adds reactions to messages based on content. Detects positive words, questions, etc. Analyzes message sentiment and adds appropriate reactions: love (❤️) for positive/affectionate messages, laugh (😂) for funny messages, question (❓) for questions, emphasize (❗) for important statements, like (👍) for general positive messages. Helps make conversations more engaging and expressive.
one_on_one_tools.when_to_use: Always runs automatically on every message to determine appropriate reactions.

parameters.returns: string - reaction type (love, like, laugh, question, emphasize) or None

one_on_one_tools.name: Group Matching
one_on_one_tools.description: Automatically creates groups or adds users to existing groups when interests match. Connects users with similar interests. When a user mentions interests, searches for other users with matching interests. If match found, either adds user to existing group or creates new group with matching users. Generates fun group names based on shared interests. Helps users find their tribe and connect with like-minded people.
one_on_one_tools.example_usage: User has 'pizza' interest → Bot finds/create group with other pizza lovers
one_on_one_tools.when_to_use: Automatically triggers when user has interests and matches are found.

one_on_one_tools.name: Conversation History
one_on_one_tools.description: Maintains conversation context across messages. Stores up to 1000 tokens of history for context-aware responses. Keeps track of previous messages in the conversation to provide context for generating relevant responses. Essential for maintaining natural conversation flow and remembering what was discussed earlier.
one_on_one_tools.example_usage: Every message → Bot stores and retrieves conversation history
one_on_one_tools.when_to_use: Always runs automatically to maintain conversation context.

group_tools.name: Vibe Check
group_tools.description: Analyzes the group chat's current energy and mood based on recent message patterns. Detects high energy, chaos, positivity, negativity, or if the chat is dead. Examines message frequency, sentiment, and patterns to determine the overall vibe. Returns Gen Z style descriptions like 'vibes are immaculate rn ✨' or 'chat is dead rn 💀'. Use when users ask about the group's energy, mood, or atmosphere. Also triggered automatically when chat is quiet.
group_tools.example_usage: User says: 'vibe check' → Bot responds with energy level like 'vibes are immaculate rn ✨' or 'chat is dead rn 💀'
group_tools.when_to_use: Use when user asks about group energy, mood, atmosphere, or how the chat is feeling. Also auto-triggers when chat is dead.

group_tools.name: Aura Reading
group_tools.description: Uses AI to generate a creative, Gen Z-style aura reading of the group chat based on recent conversations. Gives a mystical/spiritual vibe reading of the chat's energy. Analyzes recent messages and creates a fun, creative description of the group's 'aura' - like 'chaotic neutral with hints of existential dread' or 'golden hour energy with main character vibes'. More creative and mystical than vibe_check. Use when users want a fun, creative reading of the chat's energy.
group_tools.example_usage: User says: 'what's the aura' → Bot responds with AI-generated aura like 'aura: chaotic neutral with hints of existential dread'
group_tools.when_to_use: Use when user asks about the chat's 'aura' or wants a mystical/creative reading of the group energy. Different from vibe_check - this is more creative and fun.

group_tools.name: Get Lore
group_tools.description: Retrieves stored 'lore' (memories/history) about a specific topic or general group chat history. Lore is automatically created from important conversations and can be queried later. The group chat has a memory system that stores important information, inside jokes, decisions, and history. Users can ask about specific topics or get general lore. If no lore exists for a topic, returns 'no lore yet'. Use when users ask about past conversations, history, or want to know what the group has discussed about something.
group_tools.example_usage: User says: 'what's the lore on pizza' → Bot responds with stored lore about pizza discussions in the group
group_tools.when_to_use: Use when user asks about lore, history, past conversations, or wants to know what the group knows about a specific topic. Extract the topic from the message (e.g., 'lore on pizza' → topic is 'pizza').

parameters.returns: string - lore entry or 'no lore yet'

group_tools.name: Generate Catchup
group_tools.description: Creates a personalized summary for a user who has been away from the chat. Analyzes messages since they were last active and generates a catch-up summary. Perfect for users returning after being away. Summarizes important events, conversations, decisions, and highlights they missed. Use when users ask to be caught up, want to know what they missed, or ask for a summary of recent activity.
group_tools.example_usage: User says: 'catch me up' → Bot responds with summary of what happened while they were gone
group_tools.when_to_use: Use when user asks to be caught up, wants to know what they missed, or asks for a summary of recent messages.

group_tools.name: Pin Core Memory
group_tools.description: Saves the current conversation or a specific moment as a 'core memory' - an important, pinned memory that the group can reference later. Like bookmarking important moments. Core memories are special, important moments that the group wants to remember forever. They can be voted on by the group and saved permanently. Use when users want to save an important moment, decision, or conversation.
group_tools.example_usage: User says: 'pin this' → Bot saves current conversation as a core memory
group_tools.when_to_use: Use when user wants to save/pin an important moment, decision, or conversation as a core memory.

group_tools.name: Would You Rather
group_tools.description: Generates a random 'Would You Rather' question for the group to discuss and vote on. Creates fun, engaging conversations and debates. The bot generates a creative, contextually relevant 'Would You Rather' question based on recent chat context. Great for sparking discussions, debates, and getting to know each other. Use when users want a fun question, debate starter, or 'would you rather' game.
group_tools.example_usage: User says: 'would you rather' → Bot generates random WYR question
group_tools.when_to_use: Use when user asks for a 'would you rather' question, wants a debate starter, or asks for 'wyr'.

group_tools.name: Roast
group_tools.description: Generates playful, Gen Z-style roasts of a target person. Lighthearted teasing that's fun but not mean. Perfect for friendly banter in the group. The bot creates creative, specific roasts based on recent context about the target. Roasts are playful, funny, and use Gen Z slang. Can respond in different languages if requested (e.g., 'roast in telugu'). Use when users want to roast someone, tease a friend, or have playful banter. Extract the target person's name from the message.
group_tools.example_usage: User says: 'roast john' → Bot generates playful roast of john
group_tools.when_to_use: Use when user wants to roast someone, tease a friend, or have playful banter. Extract the target person's name from the message (e.g., 'roast john' → target is 'john'). Can include language requests like 'roast in telugu'.

parameters.target: required - extracted from message (person to roast)

group_tools.name: Hype Train
group_tools.description: Generates hype messages to celebrate or hype up a group member. Creates positive energy and celebrates achievements or just hypes someone up for fun. The bot creates enthusiastic, Gen Z-style hype messages celebrating the target person. Great for celebrating achievements, birthdays, milestones, or just hyping someone up. Use when users want to celebrate someone, hype them up, or show support. Extract the target person's name from the message.
group_tools.example_usage: User says: 'hype up sarah' → Bot generates hype messages celebrating sarah
group_tools.when_to_use: Use when user wants to hype someone up, celebrate them, or show support. Extract the target person's name from the message (e.g., 'hype up sarah' → target is 'sarah').

parameters.target: required - extracted from message (person to hype)

group_tools.name: Story Mode
group_tools.description: Starts collaborative storytelling mode where the group collectively creates a story. Each message contributes to the ongoing narrative. Bot continues the story based on group input. Once started, the group takes turns adding to the story, and the bot continues the narrative naturally. Great for creative collaboration and fun group activities. Use when users want to start a collaborative story or creative writing activity.
group_tools.example_usage: User says: 'story mode' → Bot starts collaborative story, group adds to it
group_tools.when_to_use: Use when user wants to start collaborative storytelling, creative writing, or story mode.

group_tools.name: Show Achievements
group_tools.description: Displays all achievements unlocked by the group. Tracks milestones, streaks, and special accomplishments. Gamifies the group chat experience. Shows all achievements the group has earned, like 'First 100 messages', 'Week streak', 'Lore master', etc. Use when users want to see their achievements, milestones, or group accomplishments.
group_tools.example_usage: User says: 'show achievements' → Bot lists all group achievements
group_tools.when_to_use: Use when user wants to see achievements, milestones, or group accomplishments.

group_tools.name: Group Trivia
group_tools.description: Starts a trivia game for the group. Asks questions that the group can answer together. Makes the chat more interactive and fun. The bot generates trivia questions relevant to the group's interests and recent conversations. Great for group bonding and fun competition. Use when users want to play trivia, answer questions together, or have a quiz game.
group_tools.example_usage: User says: 'trivia' → Bot asks trivia question for group to answer
group_tools.when_to_use: Use when user wants to play trivia, have a quiz, or answer questions together.

group_tools.name: Auto Vibe Check
group_tools.description: Automatically checks the vibe when the chat has been quiet/dead for a while. Passive feature that activates when chat activity is low. Helps revive dead chats. Monitors message frequency and automatically checks the vibe if the chat has been inactive. Returns vibe description and suggests activities to revive the chat. Use automatically when chat is dead (no hardcoded triggers needed).
group_tools.example_usage: Chat is quiet → Bot automatically checks vibe and suggests activities
group_tools.when_to_use: Automatically triggers when chat has been inactive/quiet for a while.

parameters.returns: string - vibe check result if chat is dead

group_tools.name: Ghost Detection
group_tools.description: Automatically detects inactive members who haven't been active in the chat recently. Mentions them to bring them back into the conversation. Helps keep everyone engaged. Tracks when each member was last active and identifies members who haven't been active for several days. Mentions them to check in and bring them back. Use automatically to keep everyone engaged (no hardcoded triggers needed).
group_tools.example_usage: User inactive for days → Bot mentions them to check in
group_tools.when_to_use: Automatically triggers to detect and mention inactive members.

parameters.returns: string - ghost detection message if inactive users found

group_tools.name: Temperature Check
group_tools.description: Automatically detects tension or issues in the group chat. Monitors message sentiment and suggests resolution if things are getting heated. Helps maintain positive group dynamics. Analyzes message sentiment and detects when conversations are getting tense, negative, or heated. Suggests taking a break or resolving conflicts. Use automatically when tension is detected (no hardcoded triggers needed).
group_tools.example_usage: Tension detected → Bot suggests taking a break or resolving conflict
group_tools.when_to_use: Automatically triggers when tension or negative sentiment is detected in messages.

parameters.returns: string - temperature check result if tension detected

group_tools.name: Auto Hype
group_tools.description: Automatically generates hype when celebrations are detected (birthdays, achievements, milestones). Celebrates group members without them having to ask. Makes the chat more positive. Detects celebration keywords like 'got', 'won', 'passed', 'got accepted', 'got the job', 'promoted', 'achieved', 'finished', 'completed', 'yay', 'celebrate'. Automatically generates hype messages to celebrate. Use automatically when celebrations are detected (no hardcoded triggers needed).
group_tools.example_usage: Birthday mentioned → Bot automatically generates celebration hype
group_tools.when_to_use: Automatically triggers when celebration keywords or achievements are detected in messages.

group_tools.name: Story Continuation
group_tools.description: Automatically continues collaborative stories when story mode is active. Takes group input and continues the narrative. Keeps the story flowing naturally. When story mode is active, each user message contributes to the story, and the bot continues the narrative based on the group's input. Use automatically when story mode is active and users add to the story (no hardcoded triggers needed).
group_tools.example_usage: Story mode active + user adds to story → Bot continues the narrative
group_tools.when_to_use: Automatically triggers when story mode is active and users contribute to the story.

parameters.returns: string - story continuation if story mode is active

group_tools.name: Suggest Tone Indicator
group_tools.description: Automatically suggests tone indicators (/s for sarcasm, /j for joking) for ambiguous messages. Helps prevent misunderstandings in text communication. Passive feature that runs on every message. Analyzes message tone and suggests adding tone indicators like /s (sarcasm), /j (joking), /srs (serious) if the message could be misinterpreted. Use automatically on every message to prevent misunderstandings (no hardcoded triggers needed).
group_tools.example_usage: Ambiguous message → Bot suggests adding /s or /j if needed
group_tools.when_to_use: Automatically triggers on every message to analyze tone and suggest indicators if needed.

parameters.returns: string - tone suggestion if message is ambiguous

group_tools.name: Generate Voice TLDR
group_tools.description: Automatically generates a TLDR (Too Long; Didn't Read) summary for long voice messages. Helps users quickly understand long voice messages without listening to the whole thing. When a voice message is transcribed and is longer than 100 characters, automatically generates a concise summary. Use automatically for long voice messages (no hardcoded triggers needed).
group_tools.example_usage: Long voice message (>100 chars) → Bot generates TLDR summary
group_tools.when_to_use: Automatically triggers when a transcribed voice message is longer than 100 characters.

message_operations.name: Edit Message
message_operations.description: Edit a message within 15 minutes of creation. Useful for fixing typos or updating information.

message_operations.name: Delete Message
message_operations.description: Delete a message. Can be used to remove incorrect or unwanted messages.

message_operations.name: Get Message
message_operations.description: Retrieve a specific message by ID. Useful for getting full message details including attachments.

message_operations.name: List Messages
message_operations.description: Get all messages for a chat. Useful for retrieving conversation history.

reaction_operations.name: Add Reaction
reaction_operations.description: Add a reaction to a message. Types: love, like, dislike, laugh, emphasize, question.

reaction_operations.name: Remove Reaction
reaction_operations.description: Remove a reaction from a message.

reaction_operations.name: Get Reaction
reaction_operations.description: Get details of a specific reaction.

chat_operations.name: Mark Chat as Read
chat_operations.description: Marks all messages in a chat as read. Automatically called when processing messages.

chat_operations.name: Start Typing Indicator
chat_operations.description: Shows typing indicator to users. Automatically called before sending messages.

chat_operations.name: Stop Typing Indicator
chat_operations.description: Stops typing indicator. Automatically called after sending messages.

chat_operations.name: Get Chat
chat_operations.description: Retrieve chat details including participants and metadata.

chat_operations.name: List Chats
chat_operations.description: List all chats with optional filtering by phone number and pagination.

chat_operations.name: Create Chat
chat_operations.description: Create a new chat (1-on-1 or group) and send initial message.

attachment_support.description: All message sending endpoints support attachments with base64-encoded data

fields.data_base64: required - base64 encoded file data (no data URI prefix)

categories.personalization: Features that personalize the experience based on user interests
categories.information: Features that provide information or answer questions
categories.accessibility: Features that make the chat more accessible
categories.social: Features that connect users with others
categories.memory: Features that remember and use conversation history
categories.vibe_mood: Tools for checking and understanding group energy and mood
categories.memory_lore: Tools for remembering and retrieving group history and important moments
categories.decision_coordination: Tools for making decisions and coordinating group activities
categories.gamification: Tools that add game-like elements to the chat
categories.auto_features: Passive features that activate automatically based on conditions

usage_notes.one_on_one_tools: 1-on-1 tools are always active and run automatically. They don't require explicit triggers.
usage_notes.group_tools: Group tools require explicit triggers (user commands) or auto-trigger conditions.
usage_notes.trigger_matching: Triggers are matched using LLM-based intent understanding, not simple text matching. The LLM understands user intent and selects the appropriate tool.
usage_notes.auto_triggers: Auto-triggered tools run automatically based on conditions, not user commands. They check conditions on every message.
usage_notes.extract_topic: Tools with extract_topic=true will try to extract a topic from the message after removing the trigger phrase.
usage_notes.extract_from_context: Tools with extract_from_context=true will extract information from recent messages, not just the current message.
usage_notes.method_calling: Each tool's 'method' field corresponds to a method name in the appropriate handler class. The method is called dynamically.
usage_notes.parameters: Required parameters are passed based on the tool's needs. chat_id is always required for group tools. Other parameters are extracted from message_text, from_phone, or other context.
usage_notes.api_features: API features are available in both 1-on-1 and group chats. They provide low-level operations like editing, deleting, and managing messages.
usage_notes.llm_selection: All user-triggered group tools use LLM-based selection. The LLM understands user intent and selects the appropriate tool, even if the exact trigger phrase isn't used. This makes tool selection more flexible and intelligent.
